Summary:

The patient has chronic anicteric cholestasis and chronic Budd-Chiari syndrome (BCS) complicating sarcoidosis. They are also experiencing diabetes mellitus, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and elevated γ-glutamyl transferase, ALP, normocytic inflammatory anemia, and raised angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE). Abdominal ultrasound with Doppler, abdominal CT, and chest CT were performed to assess liver function and detect any underlying conditions. The patient is currently on oral prednisolone and warfarin anticoagulation therapy. Follow-up appointments with the primary care physician and specialist providers are scheduled to monitor symptoms and report any changes.

The patient has been diagnosed with a Left cerebellopontine angle (CPA) lipoma. The primary diagnosis is a benign tumor affecting the CPA region. There are no secondary conditions. The patient's hearing is affected, with a 37-dB hearing loss in the left ear and 70% speech discrimination. No critical lab abnormalities are noted. The patient has undergone radiological examinations and has been prescribed follow-up with an otolaryngologist for a CT/MRI after the prescribed medications are administered.

Summary: A 65-year-old male with a history of smoking presented with nonischemic cardiomyopathy and ECOG PS 3. He received mechanical cardiac support with an LVAD and underwent mediastinal widening and mediastinoscopy. The patient was treated with carboplatin and etoposide, followed by pathologic examination of SCLC. He passed away six months after chemotherapy administration due to the progression of his condition.

Summary: 
The patient is experiencing carcinoma of the right breast and postradiogenic circumscribed scleroderma (morphea) which have led to radiodermatitis and cutis edema. Adjuvant radiotherapy (RTX) has been performed on the right breast and supraclavicular region. Follow-up instructions include regular check-ins with doctors, monitoring of affected areas, and avoiding sun exposure and applying sunscreen.

Summary: A 65-year-old male patient with IgA nephropathy, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and end-stage renal disease (ESRD) has been diagnosed with sensorineural hearing loss, proteinuria, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets, and microalbuminuria. He has undergone a kidney biopsy and is currently on prednisone and tacrolimus. Follow-up with a nephrologist is required.

Summary: The patient presents with a complex condition involving vascular injury in neck zone II, multiple cervicofacial lacerations, and critical lab abnormalities including low hemoglobin level and hypotension. Procedures performed include CT angiography, angiography via the right femoral artery, stent insertion, and surgery to remove hematoma. Following treatment, the patient is instructed to continue antiplatelet medication and attend follow-up appointments at the outpatient clinic.

Summary:

A 45-year-old male presented with CML in chronic phase, pancytopenia, and leishmaniasis. He is undergoing TKI therapy (hydroxyurea, imatinib, pentavalent antimonials) and has high leukocyte count, low hemoglobin level, and high platelet count. Follow up care is necessary to monitor his condition.

Summary:

A 45-year-old female patient with recurrent pneumonia, lymphadenopathy, CD hyaline vascular type, lymph node enlargement, pulmonary artery dilation, and lymph node enlargement was admitted to the hospital for evaluation and management of these conditions. Her primary diagnosis is lymphadenopathy with CD hyaline vascular type. Secondary conditions include lymph nodes, mediastinal and inguinal lymph nodes, and pulmonary aneurysm. Critical lab abnormalities include lymph node enlargement, pulmonary artery dilation, and lymph node enlargement. Computed tomography (CT) scan was performed, and medications were prescribed for her condition. Follow-up instructions were given to the patient to be checked in with the rheumatology outpatient department.

Summary:

A 35-year-old female patient was admitted to the hospital due to a severe case of central keratitis and corneal scraping. The primary diagnosis is central keratitis, while the secondary diagnosis is related to contact lens use. The patient's condition has worsened due to the presence of Acanthamoeba sp. cysts in her corneal scraping, necessitating a procedure where a specimen was inoculated for further testing.

The patient is currently undergoing treatment with alternated topical fortified vancomycin, ceftazidime, propamidine isothionate 0.1%, and chlorhexidine. Follow-up instructions have not been provided in the note.

Summary: Patient received MRI scan and hydrocortisone, levothyroxine, testosterone replacement, and DDAVP for pituitary germinoma and central diabetes insipidus. Hypospadias and hypospadias repair were performed for undescended testes. Follow-up instructions include long-term monitoring for residual disease and any signs of relapse or progression.

Summary: The patient is experiencing cognitive impairment and AD-like hypometabolic pattern. Key findings include elevated tau, ptau, Aβ1-42 levels, and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid and PET scan results. Procedures performed include MMSE, MoCA-B, CDR, global deterioration scale, cerebrospinal fluid tests, Aβ1-42 level testing, Pittsburg compound B PET scan, and F-18 fluorodeoxyglucose PET scan. Follow-up instructions are to consult a primary care provider for continued management of cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease.

Summary: The patient is experiencing pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, which requires surgical removal of the tumor. They are also experiencing fever, headache, and high blood pressure due to increased adrenaline and elevated cortisol levels. Follow-up instructions include monitoring of lesions and potential further treatment.

Initial Clinical Summary:

A 20-year-old female patient is scheduled for orthodontic treatment involving maxillary right canine removal and partial maxillary osteotomy due to bone loss and apex constrained. Post-surgical stabilization, continuous arch maintenance, and follow-up evaluations in 2012 are included in the patient's follow-up instructions.

Summary: A 45-year-old male patient presents with chest pain and lightheadedness. His primary diagnoses are exertional chest pain and pleuritic chest pain, both considered secondary conditions. He also has critical lab abnormalities including jugular venous distention and muffled heart sounds. The patient has not received follow-up instructions.

Summary: A 32-year-old woman presented with a sodium hydroxide splash injury of the left eye and symblepharon with superficial and deep corneal neovascularization. She received subconjunctival bevacizumab injection, subconjunctival bevacizumab injection, dexamethasone sodium phosphate drops, tobramycin, and prednisone 50mg, daily for ten days. Follow-up instructions include a 24-month check-up.

Summary: The patient is a 50-year-old male with stage IV pulmonary adenocarcinoma diagnosed by pulmonary adenocarcinoma and lymphadenopathy in the left neck, mediastinum, and right lung tubercle. CNS metastasis was detected via transbronchial needle aspiration biopsy, endobronchial ultrasonography, mediastinal lymphadenectomy, wedge resection of the lower lobe of the right lung by video-assisted thoracic surgery, immunohistochemical analysis, gene detection, and MRI. The patient continues on pembrolizumab treatment, remains asymptomatic, and has no further follow-up planned at this time.

Summary:
A 55-year-old male presents with symptoms of heart failure and renal artery aneurysm. His primary diagnosis is Heart failure with renal artery aneurysm and arteriovenous fistula, with a secondary diagnosis of heart failure. Elevated B-type Natriuretic Peptide (BNP) levels indicate the presence of heart failure. The patient is undergoing endovascular occlusion and will continue medications as per follow-up instructions. Follow-up with primary care physician is recommended for further evaluation and management, as well as maintaining a low-salt diet, avoiding stress or exertion, and a healthy lifestyle.

Summary:

The patient has been diagnosed with HBV cirrhosis without HDV coinfections, grade 1 oesophageal varices, and elevated ALT values. Key findings include detectable HBV-DNA levels, ranging from 5.75 to 9.2 log10, and PCR-undetectable levels. Liver biopsy and various antiviral medications have been prescribed. Follow-up instructions include a liver transplantation evaluation.

Summary: The patient has been diagnosed with multiple congenital abnormalities, including an unusual genitalia, imperforate anus, duplicated bowel loops, and duplicated recto-sigmoid colon. These conditions require specialized surgical care and follow-up management. Parents are advised to schedule regular follow-up appointments with their primary care physician and discuss further diagnostic or treatment options if needed. A healthy diet and hygiene practices should be followed to prevent complications and discomfort.

Summary:

The patient has Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) and is currently undergoing treatment for Ureteral Stones, Behcet's Disease, and Multiple Myoma. She is also experiencing high Anti-Mullerian Hormone (AMH) levels. The patient will be discharged with medications and instructed to follow up during her next routine visit.

Summary: A 45-year-old female patient presented with a paradoxical reaction to anti-tuberculosis therapy. She was diagnosed with a percutaneous lung biopsy due to suspected TB. The patient is currently on isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, pyrazinamide, and levofloxacin. Follow-up instructions include continuing on anti-tuberculosis therapy as prescribed.

Summary: A 45-year-old male presented with a 3-month history of a rapidly growing, ulcerated lesion on the right lower lip. The patient's primary diagnosis is Primary Cutaneous ALCL. Further evaluation revealed a 2-cm excisional biopsy, which confirmed ALCL. Follow-up instructions include excisional biopsy if symptoms worsen or new lesions appear, and a follow-up appointment with oncology as directed.

Summary: A 45-year-old male with a history of obstructive coronary artery disease presents with RVOT-VT with chest pain and palpitations. He underwent external cardioversion, resection of the muscular band, coronary artery bypass grafting, and subcutaneous ICD placement. Follow-up instructions include continued prescribed medications as directed, monitoring symptoms, reporting changes, and seeking immediate medical attention if symptoms worsen.

Summary: A 55-year-old female presents with oral manifestations of Crohn's disease and angular cheilitis. She has low serum iron and folate levels, and a raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate. Following external gingivectomy and vitamin supplementation, she is instructed to follow up for 15 months, monitor hematological tests, and ensure gingival recovery.

Summary:

A 65-year-old male patient with a history of dysphagia and difficulty flushing the PEG tube was admitted to the hospital for PEG tube removal and Mic-Key® button placement. During the procedure, a localized PEG-tube site pain was observed. The patient is instructed to follow up with the primary care physician within 7 days for further evaluation and management.

Summary: A 58-year-old male patient is being admitted to the oncology unit for a right posterolateral thoracotomy with excision of a right-sided chest wall mass. The primary diagnosis is CMT, a secondary condition is the presence of a right-sided chest wall mass, and there are no critical lab abnormalities. The patient has undergone a right posterolateral thoracotomy with release of the left SCM tendon and will be discharged with follow-up instructions by the oncology team.

Summary: The patient is experiencing chronic pain syndrome with failed back surgery syndrome (FBSS) and mixed pain syndrome. The primary diagnoses are neuropathic radicular pain in both legs and nociceptive pain in the lower back. The patient's condition is undergoing neuromodulation treatment with spinal cord stimulation (SCS). Follow-up instructions include continued regular appointments with the neurosurgical pain clinic for reprogramming and maintenance of the neuromodulation systems.

Summary: A clinician is treating a patient with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), Diabetes Mellitus type 2, High cholesterol, Exertional dyspnea, Visual disturbances, Night sweats, and Progressive fatigue. The patient's white blood cell count (WBC) is extremely elevated (220 × 109/L), hemoglobin is low, and platelets are dangerously low. Treatment includes leukapheresis, chemotherapy and ATRA, and the patient is instructed to continue with regular follow-up and follow-up care.

Summary: A 55-year-old male with poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma with squamous features suggestive of pancreaticobiliary primary presented with generalized body weakness, difficulty sleeping, abdominal pain, increased thirst, and urinary frequency. He was diagnosed with high calcium levels, elevated alkaline phosphatase levels, low vitamin D levels, high PTHrP levels, and normal kidney function. Treatment included CT scan, PET-CT, CT-guided biopsy, chemotherapy with cisplatin and gemcitabine, and follow-up instructions.

Summary: A 35-year-old female patient is evaluated for suspected MD and palpitations. The primary diagnosis is Muscular Dystrophy (MD) gene panel, secondary to elevated creatine kinase (CK). Other findings include palpitation. Electrocardiogram (ECG) and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) were performed, and she is currently on systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) medications. Follow-up instructions include continuing SLE medications, scheduling an appointment with cardiology for monitoring palpitation episodes, and undergoing genetic counseling for the COL6A1 variant.

The patient has been diagnosed with ZIKV infection, which is characterized by contact lens intolerance and ZIKV RNA positive in urine and plasma. No medications were prescribed, and further management was deferred. The patient should seek medical attention if future concerns related to her condition develop.

Summary:

A 45-year-old male patient is admitted with a primary diagnosis of small-cell lung cancer and a secondary diagnosis of acute idiopathic pericarditis. He also has a critical condition of purulent pericarditis and acute idiopathic pericarditis. Key findings include reduced white blood cell and neutrophil counts, elevated creatinine and blood urea nitrogen levels, and high lactic acid levels.

Procedures performed include urgent transthoracic echocardiography and emergency pericardiocentesis. Medications discharged include ertapenem. Follow-up instructions include discharging home after 8 days and resuming chemo-radiation therapy 2 months later.

The patient is diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (ptsd) and suicidal ideation, presenting with symptoms of intrusive thoughts and recurrent nightmares. She is also experiencing psychiatric disorders. The patient was discharged home with follow-up in a youth intensive outpatient program (iop) the following week, focusing on non-pharmacological methods to manage her PTSD.

Summary: 
A 55-year-old female patient presented with a history of invasive low-grade carcinoma of the appendix colonizing appendicial endometriosis. She underwent right hemicolectomy, resection of two segments of small intestine, omentectomy, bilateral ovariectomy, and peritoneal resections with HIPEC administration. Follow-up is recommended to monitor for any potential recurrence.

Summary:
The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of incomplete duplication of the right side and hydronephrosis with left hydroureter. He also has hydroureter. His critical lab abnormality is 47% split renal function of the left kidney without an obstructive pattern. He underwent Cohen's ureteroneocystostomy. The patient is advised to follow up with the physician for regular check-ups as advised.

Summary:
A 12-year-old male with a history of B-cell ALL and CNS relapse presents with ongoing leukemic blasts in bone marrow, MYC rearrangement, p53 deletion, and whole brain and spine irradiation. Induction chemotherapy was initiated, followed by double-delayed intensification and maintenance therapy. The patient has been discharged and is advised for follow-up instructions.

Summary:

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of chronic bronchitis, bronchial anthracofibrosis, and tuberculous pleuritis is admitted for follow-up due to a recent diagnosis of pleural effusion with carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) 1.37 ng/mL and granulomatous inflammation. The patient is undergoing further evaluation with bronchial bronchoscopy and pleural effusion biopsy. The primary care physician is advised to be closely followed and continue anti-tuberculosis treatment as prescribed. Follow-up instructions include regular visits with the primary care physician and continued anti-tuberculosis treatment.

Summary:

A 35-year-old male with a history of recurrent pneumonia presents with bilateral infiltrates consistent with multifocal pneumonia. The patient is diagnosed with Pneumocystis jiroveci, Cytomegalovirus, Herpes simplex virus, E. faecalis, K. pneumoniae, and P. wickerhamii. He requires IV antibiotics, multiple intubations, tracheostomy, and ongoing treatment with clindamycin, gancyclovir, linezolid, ceftaroline, ampicillin, valacyclovir, and trimethoprim-sulfa. Follow-up care is recommended with his primary care provider to ensure adherence to the treatment plan and address any concerns or changes in symptoms.

Summary:

A 35-year-old female presents with intermittent headache and hypomnesis. Elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase and cerebrospinal fluid protein are noted, indicating potential involvement of the central nervous system. High-dose methotrexate and idarubicin were administered for treatment. Follow-up instructions include close monitoring of symptoms and lab results, and the need for further evaluation if signs of neurological compromise persist.

Summary: A 36-year-old male patient with Wilson's disease presenting with multiple decayed teeth and gingivitis, including moderate-to-advanced dental caries. Key findings include decayed teeth and multiple caries. Plan includes scaling, composite filling, inlay preparation, gold crown preparation, simple extraction, and treatment of caries. Follow-up appointments with the primary care physician and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

Summary:

A 55-year-old female presented with cardiac hydatid cyst, dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, eosinophilia, and dyspnea at rest. She underwent cardiac hydatid cyst surgery and is prescribed bupivacain plain, inj. tramadol, and diclofenac sodium I.M. for further management. Follow-up with her physician is scheduled for the next week.

Summary:

The patient has been diagnosed with leiomyosarcoma, a type of cancer affecting the smooth muscle tissue. The primary diagnosis is a solid tumor at the mediastinum. The patient has also been treated with radiation therapy and radiofrequency ablation (RFA). Pain and numbness in the left upper limb, as well as enhanced and non-enhanced cystic lesions, are secondary conditions. Follow-up instructions include monitoring his condition with his healthcare provider.

Summary: A 35-year-old male patient presenting with bronchial asthma, pneumonic consolidation involving the right lower lobe, surgical emphysema, subcutaneous emphysema, air in the mediastinum, pericardium, and posterior spinal epidural space. He is on broad-spectrum antibiotics, inhalation bronchodilators, systemic corticosteroids, and high-flow oxygen. Follow-up instructions include monitoring his symptoms, following up with his primary care physician regularly, and consulting with the pulmonologist as needed.

Summary: A 50-year-old male patient with a history of rheumatoid arthritis is being discharged after undergoing two Ayurvedic treatments. His allergic skin conditions remain active, and he is advised to update his treating physician on any future allergic reactions to Ayurvedic medication.

Summary: Patient is presenting with a complex neurological condition, including Streptococcus salivarius meningitis, Antiphospholipid syndrome, cerebrospinal fluid leak (CSF-L), ventriculitis, and encephalopathy. The patient has undergone multiple procedures, including lumbar puncture, bilateral endoscopic ethmoid repair with lumbar drain placement, and a ventriculo-peritoneal shunt placement. The patient is currently on apixaban for antiphospholipid syndrome and is advised to follow up with primary care provider, otolaryngologist, and neurosurgeon as recommended.

Initial Clinical Summary:

The patient is a 12-year-old girl with a history of Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA). She has been diagnosed with Sjögren's Syndrome and Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (SJIA), complicated by a myocardial abscess (MAS) and polyarthritis with serositis. The patient's coronary arteries are dilated, necessitating IVIG, high-dose aspirin, and IV methylprednisolone. She is currently on low-dose prednisone and is scheduled for follow-up appointments with Rheumatology and Cardiology.

The patient is diagnosed with acute megakaryoblastic leukemia and recurrence of metastatic germ cell tumor. Key findings include pancytopenia, low leukocyte and platelet counts. Procedures performed include bone marrow trephine biopsy and FNA of a cervical lymph node. Medications discharged are daunorubicin and cytarabin. Follow-up instructions are to schedule further appointments to monitor the patient's condition.

Summary: A 35-year-old female patient with a history of hypothyroidism and microcytic anemia underwent colonoscopic decompression procedures for obtipation and sigmoid volvulus. The patient's laboratory results are unremarkable. Follow-up instructions include a colonoscopy and laparoscopic sigmoidectomy.

Summary: Patient presents with an infected dentigerous cyst, presenting with dull, throbbing pain and fluctuant tenderness. Enucleation of the cyst and removal of an impacted mesiodent is performed. Follow-up visits with a dental care provider are recommended to ensure complete healing and management of the infection.

Summary: A 55-year-old male with rectal carcinoma history presented with significant diffusion restriction in the frontal white matter bilaterally and the splenium of the corpus callosum on MRI. He received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Follow-up for post-discharge visit with oncologist is scheduled, and he is instructed to seek emergency care for similar symptoms.

Summary:

The patient, a 55-year-old male with a history of age-related osteoporosis, presented with a right femur fracture and restricted hip mobility due to femoral head osteolysis and osteonecrosis. He was diagnosed with Femur fracture and underwent hemi replacement arthroplasty by posterior approach with a cemented bipolar prosthesis. Post-operative care and follow-up instructions were provided for 1 year after the procedure. The patient is currently asymptomatic and has favorable outcome.

Summary: A 55-year-old male with stage IV NSCLC, EGFR E19 deletion mutation and MET amplification, is undergoing treatment with gefitinib, crizotinib, pemetrexed, and carboplatin every 28 days for six cycles followed by maintenance. He also requires regular annual clinical and radiographic follow-ups and is instructed to continue medications and treatment.

Patient has a complex medical history with abdominal pain, diarrhea, vomiting, mesenteric ischemia, and suboptimal angioplasty. The patient is also advised to follow a low-fat, low-salt diet and to contact the physician immediately for concerning symptoms. Follow up with primary care physician within one week and cardiologist within two weeks of discharge.

Summary:

The patient is diagnosed with Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome, a rare disorder characterized by abnormal blood flow and resulting in excessive growth in certain body parts. He also has secondary conditions including growth retardation, abnormal body habitus, neurofibromatosis type 1, Hemihyperplasia-multiple lipomatosis syndrome, and venous malformations. Key findings include splenomegaly and venous malformations. Procedures performed include physical examination, ultrasound abdomen, and femoral angiography. Medications were not prescribed. Follow-up instructions are regular clinical evaluations to monitor the patient's condition and for appropriate management.

The patient was diagnosed with a recurrent schwannoma arising from the middle cranial base, resulting in sunken eye and drooping of the affected upper eyelid. The patient underwent surgery to augment the eye socket with an autologous ball-shaped graft composed of diced costal cartilage, correct the lower eyelid retraction with an auricular cartilage graft, and correct the upper eyelid ptosis with a fascia lata graft. The patient was advised to avoid touching the affected eye and have follow-ups as scheduled.

Summary: A 45-year-old male presented with a history of non-seminomatous germinal tumor (NSGT) E-IB, multiple sclerosis (MS), and increased AFP levels. A left inguinal orchiectomy, subcutaneous interferon β-1a, and radiotherapy (44 Gy) were performed. GEMcitabine and oxaliplatin medications were prescribed for chemotherapy. Follow-up instructions include regular follow-up with the patient's family at their discretion.

Summary: The patient is diagnosed with Acute onset type 1 diabetes and Absolute insulin deficiency. HbA1c levels are 9.6% and 7.4%, both of which are significantly elevated. The patient is undergoing treatment with premixed biphasic insulin aspart, Miglitol, Aliskiren, and Candesartan. Follow-up instructions are not provided in the note.

Summary:

A 35-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with suspected organophosphate poisoning. Initial assessments revealed normal laboratory results and no critical abnormalities. He was administered atropine, atropine 5 mg iv bolus, 1 mg hourly infusion, and parenteral hydration. A follow-up appointment was scheduled for 6 weeks post-discharge.

Summary:

A 45-year-old female patient was diagnosed with Recurrent Ductal Carcinoma in Situ (RDCIS) of the breast. She received a Stacked DIEP Flap procedure for reconstruction. There were no critical lab abnormalities noted. The patient was discharged with no medications and was advised to follow up annually for one year. She reported a satisfactory aesthetic outcome with no complications at the one-year follow-up.

Summary: 
Patient is diagnosed with myeloid sarcoma, a rare type of cancer originating in the bone marrow. The primary diagnosis is confirmed by the presence of malignant cells in the bone marrow, and no evidence of leukemic infiltration is found in the peripheral blood or bone marrow aspirates. The karyotype is normal. Treatment includes surgical removal of the mass, radiotherapy, and two courses of high-dose cytarabine. Follow-up instructions are not provided in the note.

Summary: The patient is a 28-year-old male with a history of deliberate self-harm, presenting with neurological toxicity. He is currently experiencing pH 7.36, HCO3- 20 mmol/L, PCO2 24 mmHg, pO2 135 mmHg, Base excess -5, lactate level 2.3, and O2 saturation 100%. The patient was admitted for IV diazepam administration and pyridoxine to manage neurological toxicity. Follow-up instructions include monitoring liver function and continuing supportive care as prescribed.

Summary: The patient presents with Acute Reversible Cerebral Vasoconstriction Syndrome (ARCVS), which was initially managed with Nimodipine. Follow-up with the healthcare provider is necessary for further instructions and to ensure the patient's condition is under control.

Summary: A 7-year-old male patient is scheduled for a follow-up dental appointment to monitor the progress of restoration of carious lesions on the maxillary left and right permanent central incisors. The patient's oral health has been assessed as stable with no critical lab abnormalities noted.

Initial Clinical Summary:

A 35-year-old male patient presents with a history of pleomorphic angiosarcoma (PAIS) localized to the left upper lobe. The primary diagnosis was confirmed through a pulmonary biopsy. Secondary conditions are absent. There are no critical lab abnormalities. The patient underwent a pulmonary biopsy, which revealed the presence of PAIS. The primary plan is to administer stereotactic radiotherapy on both progressive lesions. Follow-up instructions include close monitoring of the patient's condition and regular follow-up appointments.

Summary:

A 5-year-old male presented with hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) following Norovirus GI/G II infection. Key findings include leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolysis, massive albuminuria, low complement levels, and peritoneal dialysis. Follow-up instructions include continued pediatrician visits and a healthy diet and lifestyle.

Initial clinical summary for a clinician:

A 45-year-old male patient is being discharged from the hospital after undergoing multiple procedures for wound management and muscle excision. The primary diagnoses are unclear, but the secondary conditions include necrotic muscle tissue and VSD. The critical lab abnormalities are not specified. The patient has been treated with intravenous antibiotic therapy and is instructed to continue outpatient care, maintain wound site cleanliness and cover, avoid overexertion, and seek medical attention if complications arise. Follow-up instructions include visiting the primary care physician for wound care and management.

Initial clinical summary:

A 55-year-old male patient is admitted with isolated ACTH deficiency. His primary diagnosis is isolated ACTH deficiency, with secondary conditions of low serum cortisol, inappropriately low ACTH, hyponatremia, raised ADH, and hypoglycemia. He is on pembrolizumab monotherapy and receiving hydrocortisone. Follow-up instructions include monthly outpatient care.

Summary: The patient is experiencing Topiramate induced acute myopia, persistent headaches, and normal intraocular pressure. She has been advised to attend follow-up appointments with her general practitioner and ophthalmologist.

Summary:

Patient presented with epigastric pain, vomiting, and a symptomatic cystic lymphangioma originating from the left adrenal gland. An ultrasound, CT scan, MRI, and CT-guided puncture of the cyst were performed. The patient was discharged with no further symptoms after surgery and the final diagnosis confirmed by histopathology. Follow-up instructions were given.

Summary: A 55-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital for an acute condition of Gross Hydronephrosis (GH) caused by obstruction from a kidney stone at the junction of the ureter and renal pelvis. Accompanied by renal cell transitional cell carcinoma (T2N0M0), the patient experienced abdominal girth increase, abdominal distension, intermittent nausea, and intractable hiccups. The patient also had hypertension and electrolyte imbalance. Treatment included ultrasonography, computed tomography (CT), and isotope kidney scan, Laparoscopy and open simple nephrectomy, and Hydrochloride therapy. Follow-up instructions include a proper diet and regular follow-up appointments with the healthcare professional.

Summary:
The patient has been diagnosed with sinusitis and a tumor in the spinal cord. The patient's primary diagnosis is sinusitis, which was treated with a dorsal D1 to D8 laminectomy, mid-line myelotomy, total tumor excision, methylprednisolone bolus dose, and 5.4 mg/kg dose of methylprednisolone. The patient is also being prescribed methylprednisolone and is instructed to follow up in 10 days to monitor for symptoms.

Summary: The patient is experiencing low-grade neuroendocrine tumor, CLL, and marginal zone B-cell lymphoma/chronic lymphocytic leukemia. The patient has undergone R-CHOP chemotherapy and octreotide acetate, and is currently taking octreotide acetate. Follow-up instructions include monitoring CLL and addressing any future medical concerns.

Summary:

This patient has been evaluated for a range of ear-related issues, including a congenital syndrome (22q11DS), cardiac anomalies, and conductive hearing loss bilaterally. Additionally, there are malformed ossicular chains on both sides, narrow ear canals, and dehiscent facial nerve canal on the left side. The patient underwent tympanostomy tube placement and middle ear inspection and ossicular reconstruction on the left side. The patient is advised to follow up with the otorhinolaryngologic department and seek regular audiology testing.

Summary: The patient is experiencing diabetes, hypertension, spinal cord injury, and empyema. A partial lung resection was performed for adenocarcinoma, wound culture was performed, and broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment was administered. Follow-up with the primary care physician is scheduled for regular check-ups.

Summary: A clinician is treating a patient with severe craniofacial abnormalities including scaphocephaly, brachycephaly, and total synostosis. The patient has abnormal craniofacial contour and severe osteolysis. The healthcare provider has performed a radiographic study and will provide follow-up instructions.

Summary:

A 55-year-old male with a history of squamous cell carcinoma of the clavicle underwent a contrast-enhanced CT scan, RND under general anesthesia, adjuvant chemotherapy, and FDG PET-CT. The imaging findings revealed bone metastasis. Follow-up is scheduled for regular CT scans to monitor clavicle fracture and cancer recurrence.

Summary:
A 55-year-old male patient is presenting with hypertension, high cholesterol, and coronary artery disease with surgical intervention. The patient has been discharged with dual antiplatelet therapy and is instructed to follow up with the healthcare provider as scheduled.
Summary: The patient underwent surgery and is currently in post-operative care. Follow-up sessions are scheduled at the outpatient clinic for further medical evaluations.

The patient presented with biliary colic and dyspepsia. The primary diagnosis was left hemicolectomy with end-to-end anastomosis due to diffuse thickening of the transverse colon wall along a 9 cm segment, indicating a nonnecrotizing intussusception. The patient was advised to contact the primary care physician for any concerns or questions and to schedule a follow-up appointment with the surgeon within four weeks post-discharge to monitor the surgical site and assess any further symptoms.

Summary:
A 35-year-old male with a history of biliary cirrhosis and abdominal pain presents with jaundice, hepatosplenomegaly, esophageal varices, and liver transplant as potential secondary conditions. Critical lab abnormalities include high levels of bilirubin, aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, coproporphyrin, and urophyrin. A liver transplant was performed as a procedure. Follow-up instructions include continued post-operative care and monitoring for complications.

Summary:

A 55-year-old male patient presented with subdural empyema and chronic subdural hematoma, along with Brugada syndrome. During a craniotomy, the patient was found to have a subdural empyema. The patient is currently undergoing treatment with minocycline, and follow-up is scheduled with the primary care physician for wound healing and monitoring of diabetes and Brugada syndrome.

Summary: A 3-year-old female child presented with a complex congenital disorder. She exhibited narrow chest, fused lower limbs, absent genitalia, imperforate anus, and single umbilical artery. The mother had diabetes mellitus. Laboratory tests revealed bilateral renal agenesis, absence of both kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, seminal vesicle, and urethra, as well as gastrointestinal system abnormalities. Autopsy confirmed the diagnosis. Follow-up instructions are N/A.

Summary:

A 55-year-old male patient is presenting with hypertension, left total hip replacement, and chronic convulsive syndrome. He also has necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis, autoimmune, infectious, and malignant diseases as secondary conditions. The patient is undergoing brain biopsy, and is being discharged with cyclophosphamide and methylprednisolone. Follow-up instructions include consulting a neurologist as needed.

Initial Clinical Summary:

The patient is experiencing Altered mental status, hypotension, and fever. The primary diagnoses include Immunotherapy-induced RTA, which is supported by the elevated plasma glucose, BUN, and Cr levels. Additional secondary conditions include altered mental status, hypotension, fever, and the need for an infectious workup. The patient is also at risk for developing a hyperkalemic state, necessitating close monitoring of their electrolytes. The patient is currently undergoing an infectious workup, including imaging tests such as CT, urine culture, blood cultures, chest X-ray, and transthoracic echocardiogram. The patient will follow up with nephrology and oncology as an outpatient.

A 25-year-old female patient presents with abdominal pain and tenderness in the lower right quadrant. The patient has been diagnosed with ordial torsion, a condition that requires immediate surgical intervention to prevent damage to the intestines. Following laparoscopic appendectomy, she is currently on antibiotics for potential infection. Follow-up instructions include reporting any signs of pain or discomfort to the primary care physician and scheduling a follow-up appointment.

Summary: A 55-year-old male with a complex history of back pain, chest pain, hip pain, and foot pain underwent systemic venous sampling for a suspected venous disease. Following the procedure, he was diagnosed with low phosphorus and elevated alkaline phosphatase levels, and was prescribed no medications. A follow-up appointment is recommended to monitor his condition and adjust the treatment plan as needed.

Summary: A 45-year-old male patient was admitted with Idiopathic Hypotension, which led to thrombolytic recanalization of the IH. The patient underwent a Head CTA examination, DSA examination, and surgery under general anesthesia. He is discharged with follow-up instructions to follow up 2 years later to assess the progression of the IH.

Summary: A 45-year-old male with history of musculoskeletal issues presented with severe muscle pain, elevated white blood cell count, and elevated inflammatory markers. Biopsy of the right tibialis anterior muscle revealed multifocal necrosis. He is currently on prescribed medications, advised to maintain a healthy diet, follow up with primary physician, and rest as needed. Follow-up instructions include reporting any worsening symptoms and adhering to the prescribed treatment plan.

Summary: The patient has been diagnosed with MSSA infection, bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) with severe aortic regurgitation, and ascending aortic aneurysm. They are also experiencing community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). Open-heart surgery with aortic valve replacement (AVR), ascending aortoplasty, and coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) with left internal mammary artery to left anterior descending artery were performed. The patient is on nafcillin for eight weeks and will require home health follow-up to monitor for any complications, including blood tests and symptom evaluation.

Summary: A 55-year-old male patient presented for a routine upper limb dissection procedure. No significant critical lab abnormalities were detected. Discharge instructions include follow-up with the primary care physician for any future health concerns.

Summary: A 28-year-old female presented with Listeria monocytogenes meningitis and multiple generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Intravenous amoxicillin and amikacin were administered along with phenobarbitone. Follow-up is scheduled for the outpatient clinic, with protein-conjugated Pneumococcal and Haemophilus vaccines, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prophylaxis, and monitoring for recurrence.

Summary:

The patient is a 35-year-old female presenting with Borderline Personality Disorder, Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, and Bulimic Disorder. She has been started on pharmacologic therapy for the treatment of these conditions. It is recommended that she continue with psychotherapeutic interventions, maintain a healthy diet and lifestyle, and follow a healthy dental hygiene routine.

Summary: Patient presented with a large, crusting lesion on the anterior chest wall and lymph node–positive stage MCC with metastatic involvement to the pancreas and peripancreatic lymph nodes. Adjuvant radiation therapy commenced following a multidisciplinary tumor board discussion. Post-surgery, the patient completed treatment and passed away.

Summary:

A 55-year-old female patient is being discharged with a diagnosis of nodular infiltrating papillary thyroid carcinoma, with metastatic papillary thyroid cancer identified through critical lab abnormalities. The primary diagnosis is treated with a total thyroidectomy, adjuvant radioiodine therapy, and sorafenib. Ongoing follow-up is necessary to monitor response to treatment and assess for potential recurrence.

Summary:

A 45-year-old female patient with a systemic disorder presenting with fever, weight loss, and malaise was admitted for evaluation. A skin biopsy was performed, and her laboratory results revealed low-grade and high-grade fevers, along with weight loss. The patient is currently taking topical steroids, phototherapy, and medications prescribed. Follow-up instructions include continuing prescribed medications, attending subsequent appointments, and reporting any new symptoms.

Summary:

Patient is admitted with multiple abrasions over right thigh, lacerated wound over right hand, and a deep perforated wound of the right eye. There is profound bleeding, requiring emergency evisceration. Patient is undergoing follow-up for wound healing and regular CT scans for monitoring.

Summary: A 45-year-old male patient was admitted for aortic insufficiency and ascending aortic dilatation, presenting with exertional dyspnea, coughing, and increased cardiothoracic index. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed, and the patient is instructed to follow up with a cardiologist for further evaluation and monitoring.

Leukocytoclastic Vasculitis (HSP) with pulmonary infection due to Staphylococcus aureus and Mycobacterium xenopi. Elevated C reactive protein, low albumin, low ferritin, and abnormal pulmonary aspiration smear. Post-bronchoscopy sputum examination is performed for further analysis. Colchicin and Methylprednisolone are prescribed for pain and articular swelling reduction. Follow-up is recommended to monitor for recurrence and assess renal function.

Summary:

A 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and atrial fibrillation presented with a 4-week history of fever. He was admitted for ventricular demand pacing (VVI) pacemaker implantation due to complete atrioventricular block. However, during the procedure, a new vegetation was detected on the newly implanted lead. Consequently, an open-heart surgery was performed to remove the vegetation and lead, followed by epicardial pacemaker implantation. The patient is now undergoing follow-up procedures and instructions.

Initial Clinical Summary:

The patient is presenting with a new onset of paraesthesia in the thigh region, consistent with Meralgia paresthetica. The primary diagnosis is Meralgia paresthetica, and the patient is also experiencing some secondary conditions. The critical lab abnormalities are not reported, but the patient is undergoing a Nerve Conduction Study. The patient is currently taking Pregabalin 75-mg nocte and naproxen 275-mg twice daily for pain management. The patient is instructed to follow up in the clinic 4 months after the onset of the symptom and report complete resolution of paraesthesia.
